headline: Common diabetes drug shows surprising benefit for asthma sufferers
meta_description: Semaglutide, used in Ozempic and Wegovy, linked to nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks in large UK study, offering new hope for respiratory patients.
summary_short: A diabetes and weight-loss medication appears to reduce asthma attacks by nearly 40%, according to research presented in Barcelona this week.
body:
A medication already trusted by millions for managing type 2 diabetes and weight loss may offer an unexpected bonus: significant relief from asthma attacks. Researchers analyzing electronic medical records from across the UK found that people taking semaglutide—the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy—experienced nearly 40% fewer asthma attacks compared to those on other diabetes medications. The same drug was also linked to about 20% fewer flare-ups in COPD, a serious chronic lung condition. The findings were presented this month at the European Respiratory Society Congress in Barcelona, Spain, drawing attention to a connection researchers had not previously explored in clinical trials.

Professor Chloe Bloom of Imperial College London, who led the study, emphasized that these results come from real-world health data rather than controlled experiments. Her team examined records from between 20,000 and 22,000 patients in four parallel studies, comparing those who started GLP-1 medications with those prescribed sulfonylureas, a different class of diabetes drug. Among all the GLP-1 drugs examined, semaglutide stood out as producing the strongest respiratory benefits, particularly for asthma sufferers.

Yet researchers are careful not to overstate the findings. People with asthma or COPD should not begin taking these medications specifically to treat their lung conditions, Bloom cautioned—at least not yet. The discovery hints at something deeper: that metabolic health and respiratory health may be more intertwined than previously recognized. The real next step is rigorous clinical trials that directly measure whether semaglutide and similar drugs truly improve lung outcomes when given as part of comprehensive airway disease treatment. For now, this unexpected benefit offers hope and a clear research direction for the future.
quick_facts: Semaglutide linked to nearly 40% reduction in asthma attacks
UK study analyzed 20,000-22,000 patient medical records
Results presented at European Respiratory Society Congress in Barcelona
Drug also associated with 20% fewer COPD flare-ups
Clinical trials needed to confirm findings
